item.title: Hermes Agent Skills: How Procedural Memory Works
item.description:
Hermes Agent skills are the agent’s procedural memory: markdown files that record how to do a task. Hermes writes them itself after working out a multi-step job, patches them when it hits a new pitfall, and loads one only when a task needs it. Each skill is a SKILL.md folder under ~/.hermes/skills/, in the open Agent Skills format.

Hermes Agent is the MIT-licensed agent from Nous Research, with about 256,000 GitHub stars on 21 October 2026. This page covers how its skills are made, stored, loaded, shared and cleaned up. Facts come from the official Skills System docs, the Curator docs and the v0.22 release notes, checked 21 October 2026. For the fact files and session search, see Hermes Agent memory.

item.title: Agent Workflow Memory (AWM): How It Works and Results
item.description:
Agent workflow memory means an LLM agent keeps reusable routines learned from its own past runs and follows them on new tasks. The best-known version is Agent Workflow Memory (AWM) by Wang, Mao, Fried and Neubig (CMU and MIT, ICML 2025). AWM induces workflows from past trajectories and puts the relevant ones in the agent’s prompt.

On web navigation with GPT-4, the paper reports a 51.1% relative gain on WebArena and 24.6% on Mind2Web. This page explains how AWM builds workflows, the difference between its online and offline modes, the full results, the limits found by the authors and by later work, and how to build workflow memory into an agent today. Sources: the arXiv paper, the ICML 2025 proceedings version, and the official repo, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: ReasoningBank: Agent Memory That Learns From Failures
item.description:
ReasoningBank is a memory framework for LLM agents from Google that stores lessons, not logs. After each task, the agent judges whether it succeeded, then writes down a few general reasoning strategies, including warnings from its failures. On new tasks it retrieves the closest lessons. On WebArena with Gemini 2.5 Flash, it lifted success from 40.5% to 48.8%.

The paper is “ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory” by Siru Ouyang, Jun Yan, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister and 13 co-authors (arXiv 2509.25140), accepted at ICLR 2026. It also introduces MaTTS, a way to spend extra compute per task to produce better memories.

item.title: Procedural Memory in AI Agents: Prompts, Skills, Workflows
item.description:
Procedural memory in AI agents is the agent’s knowledge of how to do things: the rules and skills that shape how it acts. For LLM agents it lives in three places: the model’s weights, the agent’s code and its prompts. Most current work on learning procedures edits the text parts, because rewriting text is cheaper and safer than retraining the model.

It’s the memory type agents use on every single step, and the one developers change most carefully. This page covers what counts as procedural memory, how research agents learn new procedures, and how to optimize prompts from feedback. For the full set of memory types, see AI agent memory explained.
